reasoning: All 7 touched files trace back to the finding. The fix itself is in Sources/AiTaskbarApp/UpdateChecker.swift:116-148, which adds pure isCheckDue and delayUntilNextCheck over an injected Calendar and clock, and in Sources/AiTaskbarApp/ViewModels/RefreshScheduler.swift:186-201, which replaces the fixed 86_400 s sleep with a delay recomputed each round. The tests are Tests/AiTaskbarAppTests/UpdateCheckDueTests.swift and RefreshSchedulerTests.swift. The docs are README.md:86 and AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md:285, and cmp confirms AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md are byte-identical. Both docs say 'once per calendar day — at launch if it has not checked today, and at the start of each new day while running', and no other lockstep doc mentions the update cadence. config.example.toml [updates] never gave a cadence, and the Localizable.strings files have no update/24h/daily wording. Public surface: the new UpdateChecker init parameters (calendar, now) and the internal RefreshScheduler updateSleeper parameter all have defaults, so the one call site at AiTaskbarApp.swift:21 builds unchanged. The new public statics are all in the app target, not a library. No persisted format changed: lastCheckKey still stores an epoch Double, so the value an existing user already has stays valid. No new dependency, host, secret or entitlement. No hidden cost: the loop still wakes at most about once a day, with a 60 s floor on the sleep. The unrequested guard 'updates.config.enabled' at RefreshScheduler.swift:187 is harmless. UpdateChecker.config is a `let` (UpdateChecker.swift:68), and checkIfNeeded already returned early when updates were disabled (UpdateChecker.swift:174). Turning updates on in Settings only takes effect after a relaunch (SettingsViewModel.swift:8-9 'relaunch to apply' banner). So a user who enables updates at runtime sees the same thing before and after the fix: nothing until relaunch, then the loop starts. The guard only stops an idle Task that could never do work. It is small and pinned by update_loop_not_started_when_disabled.
